slot.brief: Numerical where a fixed half-life must be used to find the time for a sample to fall from an initial to a final mass/activity — count the number of half-lives and multiply.

stem: A first-order reaction has a half-life of $4\ \text{min}$. How long does the reactant concentration take to fall from $0.80$ to $0.10\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$?

verdicts.working: The concentration falls by a factor of 8, or three half-lives. Time = 3 × 4 = 12 min.

working:
$\dfrac{0.10}{0.80}=\dfrac18=\left(\dfrac12\right)^3$

Independent check: The concentration falls by a factor of 8, or three half-lives. Time = 3 × 4 = 12 min.
solution:
For a first-order reaction, each half-life halves the concentration. Since $\dfrac{0.10}{0.80}=\dfrac18=\left(\dfrac12\right)^3$, this takes three half-lives.
$$t=3(4)=12\ \text{min}$$
